# Format detection

> Generated by `tools/` from the inputs in `source/`. Every statement below is backed by assembly metadata, IL, or a supplied export sample.
> Anything that could not be proven from those inputs is marked **Unknown** rather than guessed.

Spec v3 section 3. Detection runs on bytes, never on the file name. A `.zip`
that holds a plain JSON document is classified as JSON with a warning, not
rejected as a broken ZIP.

## Order of inference

```
magic bytes  ->  physical format
                      |
                      v
  embedded markers / manifest  ->  logical format
                      |
                      v
            structure  ->  variant
                      |
                      v
                 parser choice
```

## Physical signatures used

| Physical format | Signature | Where it leads |
|---|---|---|
| GZip | 1F 8B | decompress, then look for BinaryFormatter and DataSet markers |
| ZIP | `PK` 03 04, or `PK` 05 06 for an empty archive | read `manifest.json` from the archive |
| PlainJson | optional UTF-8 BOM, then an opening brace or bracket | parse, then read `manifest` or `format` |
| XML | a leading `<` | not an export family seen here |
| PE | `MZ` | an assembly, handled by the inventory phases |

## Logical markers

| Logical format | Marker | Confidence when matched |
|---|---|---|
| `Barsa.LegacyMetaExport` | GZip payload begins with the BinaryFormatter header 00 01 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF and names `System.Data.DataSet` | Verified |
| `Barsa.AiExport` | a manifest whose `format` is `Barsa.AiExport`, either at `$.manifest` in a single document or in `manifest.json` inside a ZIP | Verified |
| `AiExport.MultiProjectionPackage` | a ZIP manifest whose `packageType` is `barsa-json-export` | Verified |

The `Barsa.AiExport` literal is not a guess: `JsonExportDocumentBuilder.BuildInitialDocument`
and `JsonExportPackageWriter.WriteManifest` both write it, and
`MetadataPackageWatcher.IsSemanticProjectionManifest` reads it back.

## Warnings

_None._

## Error model

Failures are format-specific per spec v3 section 63, so a bad ZIP and a bad
GZip are not reported as the same thing: `PhysicalFormatDetectionError`,
`GZipDecodeError`, `LegacyPayloadParseError`, `JsonParseError`,
`ZipPackageError`, `ManifestError`, `NormalizationError`, `ScopeMatchError`,
`SemanticMatchError`.
